July 27, 1937.

- 3 -

China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill (Chinese)
- Unrest among workers

During the afternoon of July 26, forty representatives
of the employees of the China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving
Mill, 1099 Connaught Road, O.O.L., held a meeting in the
Underwear Makers' Union, 21 Yung Sze Fang, Kying Sze Doo
Miao, off Connaught Road, O.O.L. It was decided that
Mr. Loh Ching-dz, committee member of the local Tangpu
be requested to induce the management of the mill to
reinstate the female worker who was recently dismissed
(Vide I.R. 24/7/37) and to enforce the rules of the
agreement reached in June, 1937, concerning the improvement
in the treatment of the workers. It was further resolved
that all workers in the employ of the mill be instructed
to pay their membership fees to the union.

Local Silk Filatures - Situation

During the forenoon of July 26, eight representatives
of the local silk filature owners called at the local
Tangpu and the Bureau of Social Affairs, and requested
the authorities to petition the Chekiang and Kiangsu
Provincial Governments to remove the ban on the transport
of silk cocoons to Shanghai. The above ban has compelled
a number of filatures to close down, owing to the lack of
cocoons. The officials of the local Tangpu and the
Bureau of Social Affairs promised to refer the matter
to the City Government.

中国ABC内衣织造厂（华资）
- 工人骚动

7月26日下午，位于老闸捕房辖区康纳路1099号的中国ABC内衣织造厂的四十名雇员代表，在老闸捕房辖区康纳路旁静寺道庙永思坊21号的内衣业工会举行会议。会议决定，请求当地唐浦委员会成员罗敬之先生（Loh Ching-dz，音译）促使厂方复职近期被解雇的女工（参见1937年7月24日情报报告），并执行1937年6月达成的关于改善工人待遇的协议规则。会议还决议，指示该厂所有受雇工人向工会缴纳会费。

本地丝厂 - 局势

7月26日上午，八名本地丝厂业主代表拜访了当地唐浦和社会局，请求当局向浙江和江苏省政府请愿，解除禁止将蚕茧运往上海的禁令。由于缺乏蚕茧，上述禁令已迫使多家丝厂关闭。当地唐浦和社会局的官员承诺将此事项转呈市政府。

China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill (Chinese)
- Unrest among workers

On July 23, a female worker of the China A.B.C.
Underwear and Weaving Mill, 1099 Connaught Road, O.O.L.,
was dismissed for having absented herself from duty for
two days without permission from the Management. Three
representatives of the workers immediately brought the
matter to the notice of the local Tangpu, and requested
that the Management be instructed to reinstate the
dismissed worker.

In addition, the workers' delegates requested
the Authorities to induce the employers to abide by the
rules of the agreement reached in June, 1937 concerning
the improvement in the treatment for the workers
(Vide I.R. 16/6/37).

American Far Eastern Match Factory - Operations resumed

Operations in the American Far Eastern Match Factory,
Tseu Ka Jao, Western Chapel, were resumed on July 23, with
a normal complement of some 350 hands. About seventy
workers who were the source of the trouble have been
dismissed.

It will be recalled that this factory declared a
lockout on July 7, 1937, in consequence of a "tai-kung"

June 2, 1937.
- 2 -
China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill (Chinese)
- Strike ends

Through the mediation of the local Tangpu and the
Bureau of Social Affairs, the strike of the workers of the
China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill, 1099 Connaught
Road, O.O.L. which was declared on May 28, to enforce a
set of demands including those for the reinstatement of
ten dismissed workers and an increase of 10% in wages
(Vide I.R. 31/5/37) terminated at 2 p.m. June 1, pending
further negotiations by the authorities. Approximately
120 of the 200 workers who were involved in the strike
are operating this morning, June 2. The remainder, being
non-union members, are being prevented from resuming work
by pickets posted by the 3rd District Cotton Weavers'
Union, No.5 Ying Sih Li, Tonquin Road (Pootoo Road District).

Local Chinese Silk Filatures - Situation

Two of the four silk filatures located in the
Settlement employing 1,500 workers and sixteen of the
fifty-one filatures situated in Chinese controlled territory
employing 6,630 workers are at present operating.

Nakayama Steel Works (Japanese) - Strike situation

The strike of approximately 300 workers of the
Nakayama Steel Works, 485 Brenan Road, O.O.L., which
began on May 28, continues this morning, June 2.

中国ABC内衣织造厂（华资）
- 罢工结束

经当地唐浦和社会局调解，位于老闸捕房辖区康纳路1099号的中国ABC内衣织造厂工人于5月28日宣布的罢工于6月1日下午2点结束，以待当局进一步谈判。此次罢工旨在强制执行一系列要求，包括复职十名被解雇工人以及加薪10%（参见1937年5月31日情报报告）。截至6月2日上午，参与罢工的200名工人中约有120人已复工。其余人员因非工会会员，正受到普陀路地区通金路（Pootoo Road District）英四里5号的第三区棉织业工会所设纠察队的阻拦，无法复工。

本地华商丝厂 - 局势

位于租界内的四家丝厂中有两家（雇佣1500名工人）以及位于华界内的五十一家丝厂中有十六家（雇佣6630名工人）目前正在运营。

中山钢铁厂（日资）- 罢工局势

位于老闸捕房辖区布伦南路485号的中山钢铁厂约300名工人的罢工始于5月28日，截至6月2日上午仍在继续。

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang. Forwarded by [Signature] p.s.f.

With reference to the remarks of D.C. (Special Branch)
on the attached Special Branch report of June 21, enquiries
made at the local Tangpu Headquarters have elicited the
information that Mr. Woo Vung-paung (吳文邦 ), staff member
of the People's Training Section of the local Tangpu, has been
appointed by the Tangpu to direct the workers of the A.B.C.
Underwear and Weaving Mill (Chinese), 1099 Connaught Road,
O.O.L. in the matter of organizing a union. This appointment
was approved by the Tangpu following the receipt of a petition
from the workers for permission to organise a union, subsequent
to their strike in April 1937.

There is no doubt, however, that Mr. Woo Vung-paung
is the prime mover in the workers plan to organize this union.
His object is to embarrass the management of the A.B.C. Under-
wear Company, toward whom he entertains some ill-feeling on
account of a dispute which arose between him and the management
in the course of negotiations in connection with the strike of
workers of this factory in April, 1937.

Subject China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill (Chinese) - situation.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by 10 Lassier S.I.

At 1 p.m., June 20, a meeting was held in the preparatory
office of the Underwear Makers' Union, 21 Yoong Sze Faung,
Ching Sz Doo Miao, off Connaught Road, O.O.L., when Mr. Woo
Vung-paung(吴文邦), member of the local Tangpu, his assistant
Mr. Pan You-nung(潘有農), and twenty representatives of workers
of the China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill, 1099 Connaught
Road, O.O.L., were present. Mr. Woo Vung-paung, who presided,
stated that employees of the China A.B.C. Underwear and
Weaving Mill were under constant oppression by the management,
and in order to resist such oppression, the workers should
organize a labour union. Subsequently, the workers were
requested to contribute 20 cents each to cover the expenses
for the formation of the union. This suggestion apparently
met with the disapproval of the attendance who then attempted
to embarrass Mr. Woo Vung-paung by demanding an explanation as
to why he had not informed the workers of the arrest of a
female employee of the mill named Zee Lai-tsung(徐蘭珍) by
the Chinese police on June 19 on suspicion of being a communist,
and a labour agitator, who was released on the 20th June. The
attendance further signified its dissatisfaction with Mr. Woo's
failure to intervene on behalf of the arrested woman. At this
point, the attendance withdrew from the premises and the meeting
broke up.

It is reported that there will be another meeting on
June 29.

**Price's Candle Factory (British) - strike of workers**

At 8 a.m. June 15, the 120 employees of Price's
Candle Factory, 5 Robison Road, declared a strike as a
protest against the engagement of new hands and the
failure of the management to promote juvenile workers.
After negotiations, the management promised to give
preference to the juvenile workers when vacancies arise.
Consequently, work was resumed at 3 p.m. and the situation
is now normal.

**China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill (Chinese) -**
**dispute settled**

On June 14, an agreement was reached between the
management and the employees of the China A.B.C. Underwear
and Weaving Mill, 1099 Connaught Road, O.O.L., to mark
the settlement of the recent labour dispute which arose out
of the workers' demands for the reinstatement of ten dis-
missed labourers and an increase of 10% in wages. In order
to enforce these demands, the workers, totalling 200, went
on strike on May 28, but returned to work at the beginning
of this month on the advice of the Chinese Authorities
(vide I.R, 2/6/37).

According to the agreement, eight of the dismissed workers
are to be reinstated, while the demand of the workers for a
wage increase is to be discussed later. Other conditions
relating to the improvement of treatment and the recognition
of the workers' union were also included in this agreement.
It was signed by representatives of the management and the
employees in the Heng Zee (恒社), Rue Brenier de Montmorand,
in the presence of an official of the local Tangpu.

中国ABC内衣及织造厂（华资）-

6月14日，位于老闸捕房辖区康纳路1099号的中国ABC内衣及织造厂的管理层与雇员达成协议，标志着近期劳资纠纷的解决，该纠纷起因于工人要求复职十名被解雇劳工及加薪10%。为了强制执行这些要求，共计200名工人于5月28日罢工，但在中国当局的建议下于本月初复工（参见1937年6月2日情报报告）。

根据协议，八名被解雇工人将获得复职，而工人加薪的要求将在稍后讨论。其他涉及改善待遇和承认工人工会的条件也包含在此协议中。协议由管理层和雇员代表在当地唐浦官员的见证下，于恒社（Heng Zee），蒙莫朗德·布伦尼埃路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）签署。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, May 31, 1937

Less Red Tape!
THERE IS FOOD for some serious reflection on our Shanghai jurisdictional tangles in the disorders which occurred, under the eyes of helpless Settlement police, at the A.B.C. underwear factory off an extra-Settlement road on Chinese territory last week when riotous strikers broke windows and beat company officials because the Chinese force on hand was too small to deal with them.

The Settlement police lacked authority to step into Chinese territory and therefore they were compelled to stand by and do nothing while personal violence and destruction of property went on just beyond the ends of their noses. Their personal feelings may better be imagined than described, but they were bound by rules not of their making and they knew that to move without sanction of authority would instantly jeopardise them and perhaps provoke a political tangle no less serious because of its general senselessness.

The Chinese police, ten in number and up against an angry crowd of several hundred, could not risk death by going into action and in any case their efforts would have been futile or perhaps provocative of worse than actually happened. They had no authority to ask the Settlement police to help. By the time their riot van arrived the trouble was over and the mob dispersed in safety to itself if no one else.

Surely such a situation speaks for itself. It is outrageously ridiculous. Political red tape may be all very well in its way (though in what particular way we'd be hard put to explain), but why should it be allowed thus to encumber the processes of preserving the peace?

We know that already there are means of sending police into jurisdictions not their own, under escort of the home administration, and for employing (for example) Settlement fire apparatus in Chapei and vice versa. But somehow the machinery of arranging these things must be too complex if such affairs as that of last week can take place.

It would seem to the lay mind sufficient that in any such emergency, where one law-enforcement group finds itself up against a crisis and there are other jurisdictions' enforcement groups within call, it should be sufficient for the officer in charge of the out-numbered party to ask for help. Then let it be understood that the help is to be accorded promptly and with no necessity for further formality.

Riots don't happen in accordance with the learned deliberations of gentlemen at glass-topped desks and those in charge of dealing with such things have a store of common sense which may well be relied on.

少些繁文缛节！
上周，在中国领土上一条越界筑路旁的A.B.C.内衣厂发生骚乱，罢工者打碎窗户并殴打公司职员，而租界警察只能眼睁睁看着却无能为力，因为现场的中国警力太少，无法应付。这一事件促使我们要对上海管辖权的纠葛进行一些严肃的反思。

租界警察无权进入中国领土，因此当人身暴力和财产破坏就在他们眼皮底下发生时，他们被迫袖手旁观，无所作为。他们的个人感受可想而知，难以言表，但他们受制于并非由他们制定的规则，并且他们知道，未经当局批准擅自行动会立即使他们陷入险境，甚至可能引发一场政治纠纷，其荒谬程度虽令人费解，但严重性却不减分毫。

中国警察仅有十人，面对数百名愤怒的人群，若采取行动则不得不冒生命危险，况且无论如何，他们的努力将是徒劳的，或者可能会招致比实际发生的更糟糕的后果。他们无权请求租界警察协助。等到他们的防暴车抵达时，骚乱已经结束，暴徒们已安全散去，未伤及自身，也未伤及他人。

毫无疑问，这种情况本身就说明了一切。这荒谬得令人发指。政治上的繁文缛节在其特定方式下或许尚可接受（尽管我们很难解释究竟是何种特定方式），但为何允许它如此阻碍维护和平的进程？

我们知道，目前已有办法在本地行政机构的护送下，将警察派往非其管辖的区域，并且可以（例如）在闸北使用租界的消防设备，反之亦然。但如果像上周那样的事情仍然发生，那么安排这些事项的机制想必过于复杂了。

在外行人看来，在任何此类紧急情况下，当一个执法群体面临危机，而其他辖区的执法群体就在附近时，人数处于劣势一方的负责人只需请求援助就足够了。随后应明确理解，援助将迅速提供，无需进一步的繁琐手续。

骚乱的发生并不遵循玻璃台面办公桌旁绅士们的深思熟论，负责处理此类事务的人拥有可资信赖的常识储备。

Sir,
At 1.45p.m. 13/3/37 a coolie employed at the China A.B.C.
Underwear & Weaving Mill,Ltd,situated at No. 1099 Connaught Road,
brought to the station a letter to the effect that the weaving
department of their mill went on strike p.m. 12/3/37.
Enquiries by D.S. White and C.D.C. 293 revealed the following:-
The A.B.C.Mill No.1099 Connaught Road is situated about 300 yards
inside the Kyung Sz Doo Miau Lane off Connaught Road,and within
Chinese Controlled Territory. This Mill however, bears a S.M.C.
Number plate and has paid S.M.C. Taxes according to the Nanking
Road Office since 1925-6. A current tax receipt showing that
$125.88 has been paid to the S.M.C. on the 26/1/37, for quarter
ending 31/3/37 was seen on file at the above office.
Mr. T.C.Wong, Manager of the A.B.C. Mill was interviewed at
the mill when the following particulars were ascertained;-
The mill has a total staff of day and night workers in the various
departments of 646 workers, 231 males and 415 females.
The mechanics employed in the Weaving department of the mill
(10) in number) failed to report for night work at 6p.m. 7/3/37,
the reason for their absence being then unknown to the management.
On the morning of the 8/3/37 only 3 of the 10 mechanics on day
work reported for work in the weaving department and no intimation
was given to the management that dis-satisfaction existed.
The weaving department however, carried on short handed until
6p.m. of the 12/3/37 when the 107 female night workers also failed
to attend for work, and at 6a.m. the 13/3/37 the day female workers
also failed to attend. Obviously these workers had been influenced
by the mechanics, who had failed to report for work on the
7th and 8/3/37.
